meta.claim: defendant A: FIN-WAIT-2 (waiting for the peer's FIN) and CLOSING (waiting for the peer's ACK of our FIN) are drawn as shape-twins -- one outgoing edge each, both into TIME-WAIT -- so the two termination paths could be swapped and compressed into one
meta.construction: order-2 group swapping CLOSING <-> FIN-WAIT-2 (states 8 <-> 6), the only nontrivial structure-level automorphism of the unlabeled RFC 9293 Figure 5 graph
meta.why_it_looks_legal: both states have exactly one outgoing edge and it leads to TIME-WAIT in both; on the unlabeled graph the swap maps arrows to arrows
meta.why_it_is_not_a_symmetry: the outgoing events differ: FIN-WAIT-2 leaves on 'rcv FIN', CLOSING leaves on 'rcv ACK of FIN' -- merging 'the peer sent FIN' with 'the peer acknowledged our FIN' is a protocol error (TV 1.0 on the completion edges under the fixed reading)
